newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA DENIES TALK OF 2006 WORLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA DENIES TALK OF 2006 WORLD CUP BID.

text.p: The head of the Russian Football Union (RFS) flatly denied reports he was considering a bid to host the 2006 World Cup finals, saying on Monday that Russia had no chance of building the stadiums needed to stage the event.
"We have made no initiative, either written or verbally, to anyone," RFS president Vyacheslav Koloskov told Reuters.

"We could not take the responsibility of arranging the World Cup in 2006," he said, noting that Russia had only three stadiums seating more than 50,000 spectators compared to the minimum eight required to stage the finals.

Moscow authorities have spent millions of dollars upgrading the city's Luzhniki Olympic stadium, complete with a retractable roof. But apart from that, Russia's only very large venues are the Dynamo Moscow soccer stadium and the ageing 80,000-seater Kirov Stadium in St. Petersburg, used for first division soccer.
With money desperately short, most Russian premier league grounds, especially outside Moscow, would embarrass teams in even the lowest reaches of professional west European soccer.
